searchText: If it were me, I would name the testnet after the git commit hash of the spec it follows. That makes it very easy to correlate the network and the version of the EIP that network is targeting. As far as next step, if we are ready for vNext, then I propose everyone check out my latest PR which applies all of the changes we have been discussing and if no one disagrees we merge it and target it. The currently merged EIP I think represents what is currently on the Besu/Geth testnet (cc <@376568077950910466> to verify). > I wonder with the recent outstanding spec changes if that is still possible or not? <@!301186049323958275> I tried with the last version of geth(https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/tree/1559_test) and besu (https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/1312) and it's still possible to have a baseFee==0 at the 162 nd block without transaction (http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/block/162) the baseFee goes up and down between 0 and 1 when there is no transaction (162 == 0, 163 == 1, 164 == 0, 165==1) > If it were me, I would name the testnet after the git commit hash of the spec it follows. That makes it very easy to correlate the network and the version of the EIP that network is targeting. Do we even have a spec that's being followed? I believe most implementations are probably in advance of the spec, no? <@!376568077950910466> I still have freeze issues with this version of Geth (https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/tree/1559_test) the first time the three Geth nodes got stuck at block 478 and after restarting it stuck at block 551 (link of the last block retrieved by geth http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/block/551) . I have the freeze issue when I spam the network with legacy and eip1559 transactions I don't see any consensus issue. Restart Geth allows me to resynchronize > Do we even have a spec that's being followed? I believe most implementations are probably in advance of the spec, no? <@!552133098075193354> Currently, I have a PR for a spec that is well in advance of any implementations. Current published version of the EIP I think is *mostly* in line with the two implementations. > <@!376568077950910466> > I still have freeze issues with this version of Geth (https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/tree/1559_test) the first time the three Geth nodes got stuck at block 478 and after restarting it stuck at block 551 (link of the last block retrieved by geth http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/block/551) . > I have the freeze issue when I spam the network with legacy and eip1559 transactions > > I don't see any consensus issue. Restart Geth allows me to resynchronize <@!680337202521440470> Hmm and this didn't happen when we tested at this state? https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/commit/630cc0b4d6feeb9a8d23076d4f80d55f6b4d1696 (back before the baseFee at 0 issue was uncovered) You said the geth node is the miner- is the testnet purely geth at this point, do we know it is specific to the geth nodes? Trying to deduce where the issue is since we have no errors to work off of <@!552133098075193354> we are currently very close to the current spec https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-1559.md with the exception being that we are decrementing the baseFee by 1 when gasUsage == gasTarget (matching eth2.0 imp) > You said the geth node is the miner- is the testnet purely geth at this point, do we know it is specific to the geth nodes? <@!376568077950910466> No for the moment Besu is the miner. Besu continues to operate and mine blocks. Is it worth trying with geth as miner to rule out incompatabilities between the two? > Is it worth trying with geth as miner to rule out incompatabilities between the two? <@!376568077950910466> Yes it is planned, we will put Geth and Besu to mine soon to test both > but knowing that by restarting it works I do not think it is a issue related to the mined block. > <@!680337202521440470> Hmm and this didn't happen when we tested at this state? https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/commit/630cc0b4d6feeb9a8d23076d4f80d55f6b4d1696 (back before the baseFee at 0 issue was uncovered) <@!376568077950910466> I don't remember having found this kind of freeze before. but as we had consensus issues, sync was stopping earlier due to all of this issues

excerpts.content: If it were me, I would name the testnet after the git commit hash of the spec it follows.  That makes it very easy to correlate the network and the version of the EIP that network is targeting.

excerpts.author: matkt0
excerpts.content:
> I wonder with the recent outstanding spec changes if that is still possible or not?
<@!301186049323958275> I tried with the last version of geth(https://github.com/vulcanize/go-ethereum/tree/1559_test) and besu (https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/pull/1312) and it's still possible to have a baseFee==0 at the 162 nd block without transaction (http://eip1559-testnet.ops.pegasys.tech:3000/block/162) 

the baseFee goes up and down between 0 and 1 when there is no transaction (162 == 0, 163 == 1, 164 == 0, 165==1)
